name: e2e
description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
readmeExcerpt: # e2e [e2e](https://e2e.com?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_intro) is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test. ```ts // tests/checkout.e2e.ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/settings/billing'); await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan'); await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro'); }); ``` Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model. ## A release gate in CI A suite that gates a release must give the same result every time it runs on a commit. e2e can run that suite with no model call: - Your coding agent writes tests with exact locators and assertions. They need no model and no key. On the web, they run in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright. - An `agent.act` step that a later assertion verifies records its actions. Commit the recordings in `.e2e/cache/` and CI replays them with no model call. With `npx e2e run --strict-cache`, a recording that no longer matches the app fails the step, and no model takes over. A step that was never recorded, or whose recording has a gap, still runs live. - `expect(locator)` calls no model. With the built-in agent, `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` call the model on every run. See [Caching](https://e2e.com/docs/cache) for what replays and when. ## Quick start ```bash npx e2e init ``` `init` asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The [quickstart](https://e2e.com/docs/quickstart) covers the rest. To see a finished setup in your stack, open [`examples/`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/tree/main/examples): Vite, Next.js, Astro, Angular, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, Flutter, and .NET MAUI, each a standalone project with a passing suite. ## MCP server `npx e2e mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server over stdio. It gives a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor a live session on your app, on web, iOS, or Android: the agent sees the screen, acts on it, gets back the test line that repeats each action, and runs your suite. The server needs no model. ```json { "mcpServers": { "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["e2e", "mcp"] } } } ``` See the [MCP server docs](https://e2e.com/docs/mcp-server) for setup and every tool. ## readmeHtml:
e2e

e2e is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test.

// tests/checkout.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from 'e2e';

test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => {
  await app.open('/settings/billing');

  await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan');
  await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount');

  await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro');
});

Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model.

A release gate in CI

A suite that gates a release must give the same result every time it runs on a commit. e2e can run that suite with no model call:

  • Your coding agent writes tests with exact locators and assertions. They need no model and no key. On the web, they run in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright.
  • An agent.act step that a later assertion verifies records its actions. Commit the recordings in .e2e/cache/ and CI replays them with no model call. With npx e2e run --strict-cache, a recording that no longer matches the app fails the step, and no model takes over. A step that was never recorded, or whose recording has a gap, still runs live.
  • expect(locator) calls no model. With the built-in agent, agent.assert, agent.waitFor, and agent.extract call the model on every run.

See Caching for what replays and when.

Quick start

npx e2e init

init asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The quickstart covers the rest.

To see a finished setup in your stack, open examples/: Vite, Next.js, Astro, Angular, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, Flutter, and .NET MAUI, each a standalone project with a passing suite.

MCP server

npx e2e mcp is a Model Context Protocol server over stdio. It gives a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor a live session on your app, on web, iOS, or Android: the agent sees the screen, acts on it, gets back the test line that repeats each action, and runs your suite. The server needs no model.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["e2e", "mcp"] }
  }
}

See the MCP server docs for setup and every tool.

Packages

Core

Package What it does
e2e The SDK, runner, and CLI.
@e2e-dev/core Drives a browser or a device from your own program, with an optional agent and no test runner. e2e is built on it.
@e2e-dev/web Browser engine: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright.
@e2e-dev/mobile iOS and Android engine: simulators and emulators through agent-device.
@e2e-dev/desktop Desktop engine, a prototype: native apps on macOS through agent-desktop.
@e2e-dev/decision Decision-model executors for bounded semantic actions and assertions, and decisionFilter(), which leaves out the tests a pull request is unlikely to affect.
@e2e-dev/acp Runs agent steps on your own coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) over the Agent Client Protocol.

Integrations

Package What it does
@e2e-dev/browser-run Cloudflare Browser Run hosted Chromium for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/kernel Kernel hosted browsers for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/notte Notte cloud browsers for the web engine, one session per test attempt.
@e2e-dev/lightpanda Lightpanda, the open-source headless browser, started per run for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/moli Local Moli browsers with on-demand layout and screenshots, started per worker slot for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/smol smol machines browsers for the web engine: by default, each attempt branches a warm Chromium microVM.
@e2e-dev/testmu TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Android emulators, iOS simulators, and real devices for the mobile engine, and hosted Chrome and Edge for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/e2b E2B sandboxes: Android 16 for the mobile engine, and Chromium for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/browserstack BrowserStack App Automate real Android and iOS devices for the mobile engine.
@e2e-dev/limrun Limrun hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for mobile tests.
@e2e-dev/revyl Revyl hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for the mobile engine.
@e2e-dev/eas Expo Simulators hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for the mobile engine.
@e2e-dev/github Reporter that posts results as a pull request comment.
@e2e-dev/html-reporter Reporter that writes the run as one HTML page, with steps, screenshots, and video.

Community

See Community packages for third-party integrations and how to add yours.

Documentation

e2e.com/docs. The e2e package ships every page, so coding agents can read them offline in node_modules/e2e/docs.

Join us

Join us in changing how software gets tested. We are hiring.

Questions? Ask on Discord. Issues are for bugs and feature requests.

Want to hack on e2e? See Contributing. We prefer an issue or a Discord discussion before a pull request.

Security

Please don't open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Follow SECURITY.md and report them to security@e2e.com.

Telemetry

The CLI sends anonymous usage data, such as which commands and engines run and where runs fail, but no test content, app content, or credentials. Opt out with npx e2e telemetry disable or E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. Telemetry lists every field.

Status

Note

e2e is in active development on the way to 1.0. APIs and config can still change between minor releases.

releases.name: @e2e-dev/testmu@0.0.7
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- [#1975](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1975) [`1676981`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/1676981ab76fd7a8b7262057a74b320545b0e3bb) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Update agent-device to 0.21.42. On iOS, `device.dismissKeyboard()` no longer presses the keyboard's Hide Keyboard or Done key: an iPad keyboard now goes away by the same short drag as an iPhone one. Pressing Enter sends one Return to the focused input, a fill reaches only the input a tap at that point reaches, and a command on a session whose simulator was deleted fails at once instead of waiting about 20 seconds. A fill on iOS is also a little faster.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source AI testing framework built on Playwright for generating and executing end-to-end tests.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: e2e is an AI-native testing framework that automates the creation and execution of end-to-end web and mobile tests. It leverages Playwright under the hood to interact with applications while using large language models to dynamically generate test scripts based on natural language descriptions. The system can interpret user flows, generate the necessary assertions, and execute them across different browser environments. By integrating AI into the testing pipeline, it reduces the manual maintenance overhead typically associated with brittle test selectors.
keyFeatures: AI Test Generation: Translates plain English descriptions of user flows into executable Playwright test code.
Playwright Foundation: Built on top of the robust Playwright engine for reliable cross-browser automation.
Self-Healing Selectors: Uses AI to dynamically identify UI elements, reducing failures when DOM structures change.
Cross-Platform Testing: Supports automated testing across both web applications and mobile web environments.
Framework Agnostic: Tests the rendered application independently of the underlying frontend framework.

useCases.title: Automated Regression Testing
useCases.description: Continuously verify that critical user journeys remain functional after code deployments.

useCases.title: Test Suite Bootstrapping
useCases.description: Rapidly generate a baseline suite of end-to-end tests for a legacy application without existing coverage.

useCases.title: Non-Technical QA Automation
useCases.description: Allow product managers and QA analysts to write functional tests using natural language.

useCases.title: Cross-Browser Verification
useCases.description: Ensure consistent application behavior across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox engines.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: QA engineers, software developers in test (SDETs), and full-stack developers looking to modernize their testing infrastructure. Users should be familiar with end-to-end testing concepts and Node.js environments.
